stimulus.source_note: Emancipation Proclamation, as issued January 1, 1863. Public domain. The figure shows the cover of the printed proclamation (published September 22, 1862).
stimulus.text:
“That on the first day of January, in the year of our Lord one thousand eight hundred and sixty-three, all persons held as slaves within any State or designated part of a State, the people whereof shall then be in rebellion against the United States, shall be then, thenceforward, and forever free . . .”

—Emancipation Proclamation, as issued January 1, 1863

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Lincoln issued the proclamation as a war measure after Antietam. Its most important military effect was to

options.text: allow Black men to enlist in the Union army.
free every enslaved person in the country at once.
options.misconception: Background: the proclamation freed no one where the Union already held power, and it covered only rebel states.

options.text: end the Union blockade of Southern ports.
options.misconception: Background: the blockade continued and grew tighter until the end of the war.
Background: Gettysburg was fought six months later, in July 1863.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the proclamation opened large-scale enlistment of Black soldiers, about 180,000 men.
rationales.B: Background: the proclamation freed no one where the Union already held power, and it covered only rebel states.
rationales.C: Background: the blockade continued and grew tighter until the end of the war.
rationales.D: Background: Gettysburg was fought six months later, in July 1863.
rationales.general:
1. The proclamation was a war measure, so ask what it did for the war effort.
2. It declared that Black men could serve, and they did, in large numbers.
3. Background from the books: about 180,000 Black men served in the Union army.
4. It also closed the door to European help, since Britain and France would not back a slaveholders’ cause.
Remember: a war measure is judged by what it adds to the army.
